sapience_notes.note: In Lean 4, adding a deprecated alias that retains a renamed declaration's original bare name does NOT avoid an 'Ambiguous term' error for modules that open both the aliasing namespace and the namespace holding the same-named declaration. Lean reports the ambiguity whether the second interpretation is a def or an alias, so the standard rename-with-alias courtesy measurably reinstates the very defect a collision-driven rename is fixing.

BimodalLogic's 'API Documentation' GitHub Actions workflow fails from an out-of-memory kill during the doc-gen4 build, not from srcUri.github misconfiguration. The failure log carries exactly two error classes: 13 'resource exhausted (error code: 12, cannot allocate memory)' lines and one 'build failed', with no URI, git-remote or configuration error. The srcUri.github targets the failure summary names are the cheap git-subprocess jobs that happened to be in flight when memory ran out, which is why GitHub attributes the failure to them. The task record and specs/ROADMAP.md both carried the wrong srcUri diagnosis.

Lake 5.0.0 exposes no --jobs/-j option (-j returns 'unknown short option'), and leanprover-community/docgen-action runs its lake build inside the action's own scripts/build_docs.sh, which a workflow cannot pass arguments to (the action's build-args input reaches lean-action's project build only). Serializing a doc build to reduce its memory footprint therefore requires vendoring the action's steps, not a flag.

BimodalLogic's scripts/readme-lint.sh compares a README's '*Last verified: YYYY-MM-DD*' stamp against 'git log -1 --format=%cs -- <dir>', the directory's last COMMIT date. A commit anywhere in a directory subtree therefore makes that directory's README stamp stale even when the commit changes nothing the README describes. Consequence for any task touching a .lean file: the gate passes before the commit and fails after it, so the stamp refresh must be budgeted as part of the same change rather than discovered at the final gate.

BimodalLogic's .claude/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh has a V10 file_scope-containment guard (--task opt-in) that silently drops any pathspec not contained in the task's declared file_scope in specs/state.json, with a WARN. The sanctioned route when an agent legitimately needs a path the creation-time file_scope did not anticipate is the proposed_file_scope array in .return-meta.json, which postflight forwards to update-task-status.sh --file-scope-add -- not overriding the guard and not editing state.json directly.
